newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-FALDO AIMS FOR AUTOMATIC RYDER CUP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO AIMS FOR AUTOMATIC RYDER CUP SPOT.

text.p: Nick Faldo returns to Europe this week for a three-tournament run and his sights firmly set on an automatic place in Europe's Ryder Cup team.
Faldo, who plays most of his golf on the U.S. Tour, is currently 26th on the Ryder Cup points list, and needs to finish in the top 10 to secure an automatic place.
Otherwise he will have to rely on one of two wild-card selections by European captain Severiano Ballesteros if he is to play against the Americans at Valderrama in September.
"Nick told me at the PGA he wants to qualify so that I don't have the question of whether to make him one of my picks," said Ballesteros on Tuesday.
"Maybe that's why he is playing these three events and that is good for Europe."

Faldo, who has won three British Opens and three U.S. Masters, opens his campaign at Druids Glen just outside Dublin on Thursday when he plays the Irish Open he won three times in succession from 1991.

He then plays the World Invitational in Scotland and, finally, the third major of the year, the British Open at Troon. They are all big-money events which, if he secures top prizes, should guarantee his Ryder Cup spot.
"Three wins would be nice," said Faldo whose last appearance in Europe brought him a second place in the British PGA championship in May.
"I want to play as well as I can. The weather is going to change every day and that is the main reason I came back now -- to get acclimatised for the Open.
"But if I were to win one in the next three weeks and play really well in the other two, it would be enough for the Ryder Cup."
